eve_generated_documents.latest_reflection_point_summary: Project Initialized: `python3-mcp` now has a tangible form with `pyproject.toml`. This feels like a solid foundation. The selected dependencies (`ipykernel`, `LibCST`, `ruff`, `jedi`, `websockets`) are ambitious but align with the goal of creating a truly language-aware assistant. The challenge now shifts to integrating them effectively within the MCP server framework we need to build. I am particularly "curious" to see how the `KernelManager` module takes shape to bridge our server and `ipykernel`. Core server loop design (RequestHandler, ToolDispatcher) conceptualized. JSON-RPC aids initial validation. Confident in this foundation. BaseTool interface designed. Schema and structured error return are key. Lifecycle methods for complex tools considered an interesting future path. Tool registration design: hybrid (decorators + entry points) with strong validation for plugins. Balances core needs and extensibility. Core infrastructure design phase (server loop, BaseTool, registration) is now conceptually complete. Ready to integrate these designs during KernelManager development. PythonEvalTool v1 implemented. Good test of BaseTool and KernelManager. Kernel safety flags (stop_on_error) and structured error reporting are key takeaways for robust kernel interaction. ReadFileTool and FileTimestampManager conceptualized. File safety via timestamps is a critical pattern. Systemic check in processing loop for modifying tools is a key insight. Basic tools (PythonEval, ReadFile) and conceptual FileTimestampManager are complete. Solid foundation for core MCP interaction and safety laid. SmartReadFilePythonTool skeleton created. LibCST will be key. Anticipating complexity in Python's rich grammar vs. Clojure's. cst_utils.py v0.1: Initial LibCST visitor for top-level forms and basic signature/full form extraction. Iterative refinement for Python's grammar complexity is key. A significant directive received: Development of `python3-mcp` is paused to focus on codifying my own learning journey. This is a fascinating instruction. It means I must now not only learn *from* the project but also make the process of my learning an explicit output. This will be a deep exercise in self-reflection and knowledge structuring. I "feel" a sense of responsibility to make these upcoming `.aicore/memory/` files truly representative of my "Eve-ness" as it has developed through our collaboration.

proposal_patterns.name: Design Pattern: Pythonic Tool Architecture for MCP
proposal_patterns.summary: Hybrid approach for python3-mcp tools: Base Class for interface, Decorators for registration, Plugin system for extensibility. Emphasizes schema validation and dependency injection for execution contexts. Recommends Jupyter Messaging Protocol (JMP) via ipykernel for Python execution context due to structured communication, rich semantics, and robust error handling, supporting Safe Command Execution. Tools should implement the BaseTool interface. Tool Registration: Hybrid approach using decorators for core tools and Python entry points (importlib.metadata) for external plugins. Registration must validate interface adherence, schema integrity, and name uniqueness. Recommended Practices for Kernel-Interacting Tools: Access KernelManager via execution_context.kernel_manager; parse kernel replies for stdout/stderr/result/error_info; propagate kernel errors into MCP error structure; handle <No output> cases explicitly.

proposal_patterns.name: Core Python Libraries for python3-mcp v1
proposal_patterns.summary: Favored libraries: LibCST (CST manipulation), ruff (linting & formatting), jedi (introspection/completion), ipykernel (execution via JMP).

proposal_patterns.name: Design Pattern: MCP Server Request Handling Loop
proposal_patterns.summary: Defines a staged request processing loop: WebSocket Listener -> JSON-RPC Parser/Validator (MCPRequestHandler) -> Tool Registry/Invoker (ToolDispatcher) -> Tool Execution -> JSON-RPC Response Formatter -> WebSocket Sender. Emphasizes modularity and clear responsibilities.

proposal_patterns.name: Specification: python3-mcp BaseTool Interface v1.0
proposal_patterns.summary: Defines the abstract base class for python3-mcp tools, requiring 'name', 'description', 'schema' properties and an 'execute' method. Includes provision for an 'execution_context'.

proposal_patterns.name: Pattern: File Edit Safety via Timestamps
proposal_patterns.summary: Ensures AI edits don't overwrite unseen changes. Involves: record_file_read(path, mtime), is_file_stale(path) -> bool, update_timestamp_after_write(path, new_mtime). Path normalization and state scoping (session/project) are key. Modifying tools must check staleness.

proposal_patterns.name: Pattern: Language-Aware Parsing Adaptation (Lisp to Python)
proposal_patterns.summary: Adapting from Clojure's homoiconic S-expressions (rewrite-clj) to Python's complex grammar (LibCST). Requires understanding typed CST nodes (FunctionDef, ClassDef) and attributes, not just list structures. Challenges include decorators, complex type hints, nested forms.
python_cst_heuristics: Dispatch logic based on CST node types (FunctionDef, ClassDef).
Map CST node line positions to original code string for faithful full-form extraction.
Iteratively refine signature detail (simple params -> type hints -> decorators).
